outcome: Other adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes
cohort: 583 women in their first subsequent singleton delivery following a second-stage cesarean delivery
finding: There was no significant difference in the rate of spontaneous preterm birth < 37 weeks in subsequent pregnancies following second-stage cesarean delivery with the push method compared to the reverse breech extraction method.
mod_finding: The study found no significant difference in preterm birth rates in subsequent pregnancies for women who had a second-stage cesarean delivery with either the 'push' method or reverse breech extraction.
